context: Corrected options, checked on main 2ad85de. Your rule says each layer proves a change once, and the batch's CI run is the one full run. The builder instructions add one exception: a lane that touches lint/, hooks/ or actions/ runs the whole CI job locally first, which takes about 90 minutes. The reason was test fixtures that copied a hand-picked list of files, so a change in one suite broke another. PR #633 removed that cause, because fixtures now copy whatever git lists. Whether those cross-suite reds still happen is unmeasured.

options.gain: Saves about 90 minutes per lane. No false reds from the container that teach lanes to scroll past failures.
options.how: The batch CI run is the only full run, as your rule says.
options.label: Drop the exception
options.lose: A cross-suite break shows up in the batch. That lane is dropped, and the rest merge after one re-run (about 45 minutes).

options.how: A new tool maps files to the suites that read them.
options.label: Run only the suites that read the files the lane touched
options.lose: The mapping tool doesn't exist yet.

options.how: The rule text names this one exception.
options.label: Keep it, as a named exception in the rule
options.lose: The same suites run twice, plus the 90 minutes and the container noise.

ref: c69 (test fixtures stop listing files; a lane can run a whole CI job), PR #633
title: Should a lane still run the full CI job (about 90 minutes) before it sends?
why: The cause of the exception is fixed, and a red batch already has a cheap, ruled recovery. If batches start going red on cross-suite breaks again, that incident would justify (b).
